### CVE-2026-0595 — Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') in GitLab
- Assigner: GitLab | Published: 2026-02-11 | Updated: 2026-02-26 | Max CVSS: 7.3
- CWE: CWE-79 CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 7.3 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 13.9 before 18.6.6, 18.7 before 18.7.4, and 18.8 before 18.8.4 that, under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user to add unauthorized email addresses to victim accounts through HTML injection in test case titles.

**solutions:** Upgrade to versions 18.6.6, 18.7.4, 18.8.4 or above.

Affected:
- GitLab / GitLab: affected 13.9 <18.6.6 (semver); affected 18.7 <18.7.4 (semver); affected 18.8 <18.8.4 (semver)

Credits: Thanks [joaxcar](https://hackerone.com/joaxcar) for reporting this vulnerability through our HackerOne bug bounty program

References:
- https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/issues/584975 [issue-tracking,permissions-required]
- https://hackerone.com/reports/3486862 [technical-description,exploit,permissions-required]
- https://about.gitlab.com/releases/2026/02/10/patch-release-gitlab-18-8-4-released/

### CVE-2026-61559 — @zereight/mcp-gitlab Vulnerable to Server-Side Request Forgery
- Assigner: GitHub_M | Published: 2026-09-15 | Updated: 2026-09-17 | Max CVSS: 9.6
- CWE: CWE-918 CWE-918: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 9.6 CRITICAL `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=poc, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

`@zereight/mcp-gitlab` is a Model Context Protocol server for GitLab. Starting in version 0.0.1 and prior to version 2.1.27, when the environment variable `ENABLE_DYNAMIC_API_URL=true` is set, the server reads the `X-GitLab-API-URL` HTTP request header and uses it as the base URL for all outbound GitLab API calls made within that request. The server validates that the value is a well-formed URL (`new URL(dynamicApiUrl)`) but applies no allowlist or hostname restriction. The server then attaches the victim's `Private-Token` to every outbound fetch that uses the redirected URL. Any caller who can reach the HTTP transport can set `X-GitLab-API-URL` to an attacker-controlled host. The next GitLab API call the server makes delivers the victim's token to that host. Version 2.1.27 contains a patch.

Affected:
- zereight / gitlab-mcp: affected >= 0.0.1, < 2.1.27

References:
- https://github.com/zereight/gitlab-mcp/security/advisories/GHSA-2h44-8472-frjj [x_refsource_CONFIRM]
- https://github.com/zereight/gitlab-mcp/pull/625 [x_refsource_MISC]
- https://github.com/zereight/gitlab-mcp/commit/6ffb4cc70706fd05b1ab80901676bc2998b6db6d [x_refsource_MISC]
- https://github.com/zereight/gitlab-mcp/releases/tag/v2.1.27 [x_refsource_MISC]

### CVE-2026-61560 — @zereight/mcp-gitlab's unauthenticated arbitrary file read via `upload_markdown` enables PAT exfiltration and full account takeover
- Assigner: GitHub_M | Published: 2026-09-15 | Updated: 2026-09-16 | Max CVSS: 9.8
- CWE: CWE-22 CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 9.8 CRITICAL `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=poc, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=total

`@zereight/mcp-gitlab` is a Model Context Protocol server for GitLab. Prior to version 2.1.27, the SSE transport mode (`SSE=true`) exposes all MCP tools without any authentication. The `upload_markdown` tool reads arbitrary files from the server's local filesystem via an unsanitized `file_path` parameter and uploads them to a GitLab project. Combined, any unauthenticated network-reachable attacker can read `/proc/self/environ` to steal the server's `GITLAB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN` and achieve full GitLab account takeover. This is the default configuration for Docker deployments. Version 2.1.27 contains a patch.

Affected:
- zereight / gitlab-mcp: affected < 2.1.27

References:
- https://github.com/zereight/gitlab-mcp/security/advisories/GHSA-cv3r-c5h8-f4g5 [x_refsource_CONFIRM]
- https://github.com/zereight/gitlab-mcp/pull/482 [x_refsource_MISC]
- https://github.com/zereight/gitlab-mcp/pull/554 [x_refsource_MISC]
- https://github.com/zereight/gitlab-mcp/pull/622 [x_refsource_MISC]

### CVE-2026-61568 — @zereight/mcp-gitlab: DNS rebinding reaches local Streamable HTTP MCP transport
- Assigner: GitHub_M | Published: 2026-09-15 | Updated: 2026-09-16 | Max CVSS: 9.6
- CWE: CWE-350 CWE-350: Reliance on Reverse DNS Resolution for a Security-Critical Action
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 9.6 CRITICAL `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

`@zereight/mcp-gitlab` is a Model Context Protocol server for GitLab. Versions prior to 2.1.30 expose the Streamable HTTP MCP endpoint without an effective Host or Origin allowlist. A malicious web page can use DNS rebinding to route browser requests to a victim's local MCP listener while preserving an attacker-controlled `Host` and `Origin`. The server accepts those headers and reaches the MCP initialization path instead of rejecting the request at the HTTP boundary. Version 2.1.30 contains a patch.

Affected:
- zereight / gitlab-mcp: affected < 2.1.30

### CVE-2026-92470 — Missing Authorization in GitLab

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab EE affecting all versions from 18.7 before 19.2.7, 19.3 before 19.3.3, and 19.4 before 19.4.1 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user to access sensitive CI/CD variable values from debug-mode job traces through the Duo AI troubleshooting feature due to missing authorization checks.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 19.1 before 19.2.8, 19.3 before 19.3.5, and 19.4 before 19.4.2  that, under certain conditions, could have allowed an authenticated user to execute arbitrary JavaScript in the context of other users' browser sessions via a specially crafted repository, due to improper sanitization of HTML attributes in syntax-highlighted output.

### CVE-2026-100741 — Improper Neutralization of Directives in Dynamically Evaluated Code ('Eval Injection') in hMailServer
- Assigner: GitLab | Published: 2026-09-27 | Updated: 2026-09-28 | Max CVSS: 9.8
- CWE: CWE-95 CWE-95: Improper Neutralization of Directives in Dynamically Evaluated Code ('Eval Injection')
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 9.8 CRITICAL `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=total

Eval injection in the JScript event-script dispatcher in Progressive Robot Ltd's hMailServer, versions 6.0.0 through 6.3.3 on Windows, allows a remote, unauthenticated attacker to run arbitrary JScript inside the hMailServer service process, with the privileges of the service account, via a password containing a backslash followed by an apostrophe, sent in any logon (SMTP AUTH, POP3, IMAP) that names an existing, active account. Exploitation requires a non-default configuration: event scripting enabled (off by default), the script language set to JScript (the default is VBScript), and an OnClientValidatePassword handler defined in the event script. The server wrote event values into the handler call as JScript string literals, escaping the apostrophe but not the backslash, so such a value closes the literal and the rest of it is parsed as script. The same flaw is reachable by a remote POP3 server through the message UID it returns, where an OnExternalAccountDownload handler is defined, and by a remote SMTP server through the error reply it rejects a delivery with, where an OnDeliveryFailed handler is defined. Before 6.2.25 the injected script can create any COM object, and from 6.2.25 it can with the default ScriptAllowedObjects value of '*'; WScript.Shell among them gives command execution as the service account. VBScript event scripts and the Linux builds of Progressive Robot Ltd's hMailServer are not affected.

**solutions:** Upgrade to hMailServer 6.3.4. Until then, write the event handlers in VBScript, or define no OnClientValidatePassword, OnExternalAccountDownload or OnDeliveryFailed handler in JScript.

Affected:
- Progressive Robot Ltd / hMailServer: affected 6.0.0 <6.3.4 (semver)

Credits: Found in the hMailServer project's own code review (Progressive Robot Ltd)

### CVE-2026-103010 — Heap-based Buffer Overflow in hMailServer
- Assigner: GitLab | Published: 2026-10-08 | Updated: 2026-10-08 | Max CVSS: 7.8

Heap-based buffer overflow in the legacy Blowfish decryption routine (BlowFishEncryptor::DecryptFromString) in Progressive Robot hMailServer 6.0.0 through 6.3.3 on Windows allows a local interactive user with no hMailServer credentials to write bytes of their choosing past the end of a 255-byte heap buffer in the hMailServer service process, which runs as LocalSystem by default. ### CVE-2026-103647 — Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') in hMailServer
- Assigner: GitLab | Published: 2026-10-08 | Updated: 2026-10-08 | Max CVSS: 8
- CWE: CWE-79 CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

Cross-site scripting in the webmail of Progressive Robot hMailServer 6.3.2 through 6.3.5 allows a remote attacker who can send a user an encrypted message to run script in the webmail's origin with that user's session. When the webmail decrypted an S/MIME message (from 6.3.2) or an OpenPGP message (from 6.3.4) in the browser, it offered each decrypted attachment as a blob URL of the media type the message declared for it. A click saved the file, but if the user opened the attachment in a new tab, a part declared as text/html was rendered as a document of the webmail's origin and its script could read the mailbox, send mail and change the account through the REST API. The webmail is served only when the REST API is enabled, which it is not by default.

**solutions:** Upgrade to hMailServer 6.3.6, which hands every decrypted attachment to the browser as application/octet-stream so that it is only ever saved. Until then: keep the REST API off (RestApiPort 0, the default), or tell webmail users not to open decrypted attachments in a new tab.

Affected:
- Progressive Robot Ltd / hMailServer: affected 6.3.2 <6.3.6 (semver)

### CVE-2026-103649 — Synchronous Access of Remote Resource without Timeout in hMailServer
- Assigner: GitLab | Published: 2026-10-08 | Updated: 2026-10-08 | Max CVSS: 7.5
- CWE: CWE-1088 CWE-1088: Synchronous Access of Remote Resource without Timeout
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 7.5 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=partial

Missing network timeouts in the Linux builds of Progressive Robot hMailServer 6.3.0 through 6.3.5 allow a remote attacker to hold server threads indefinitely and so stop outbound mail delivery (denial of service). The server set its socket timeouts in the form Windows takes, which Linux refuses, and its HTTPS clients read without a deadline, so a peer that accepts a connection and then sends nothing held the waiting thread for as long as the connection stayed open. The MTA-STS policy fetch, enabled by default, is made during outbound delivery to mta-sts.<recipient domain>, so anyone who can make the server deliver mail to a domain they control - for example as the envelope sender of a message that bounces - can hold delivery threads until outbound delivery stops. The same flaw affects the DANE TLSA query, the OAuth2 token request, the ACME client, and the ManageSieve and metrics listeners, which a silent client stops from serving anyone else. Windows builds are not affected.

**solutions:** Upgrade to hMailServer 6.3.6, where every one of these requests and listeners has a deadline on Linux as on Windows. Until then, on Linux: set MtaStsEnabled to 0 if outbound delivery stalls, keep ManageSieve and the metrics listener off or reachable only from trusted networks, and restart the service to release held threads.

Affected:
- Progressive Robot Ltd / hMailServer: affected 6.3.0 <6.3.6 (semver)

Credits: Found in the hMailServer project's own static-analysis review (Progressive Robot Ltd)

### CVE-2026-104658 — Reliance on Untrusted Inputs in a Security Decision in hMailServer
- Assigner: GitLab | Published: 2026-10-08 | Updated: 2026-10-08 | Max CVSS: 7.8
- CWE: CWE-807 CWE-807: Reliance on Untrusted Inputs in a Security Decision
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 7.8 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

The Linux live-update apply helper (hmailserver-update) of Progressive Robot hMailServer 6.3.4 and 6.3.5 runs as root on a request file written by the unprivileged hmailserver service account, and took from that request the program used to verify an AppImage update's signature and the systemd unit to stop before reading the service account's files. An attacker who already runs code as the hmailserver service account, for example through another flaw in the mail server, can therefore have arbitrary code executed as root, on any Linux installation where the live update's path unit is active - the default for the project's .deb and .rpm packages - and on AppImage installations run under that unit.

**solutions:** Upgrade to hMailServer 6.3.6, whose helper takes the unit and the AppImage only from its own root-owned command line, refuses an AppImage request where that names none, confirms that the server has stopped, and verifies, runs and installs only copies it made after the stop, readable by root alone until they have verified. Install 6.3.6 with the package manager (apt or dnf) rather than through the live update. An AppImage run under the path unit keeps the helper script copied to /usr/lib/hmailserver/ when its update units were installed, which the AppImage's own update does not replace: copy 6.3.6's script there and give it --image in a drop-in for hmailserver-update.service. Until then: systemctl disable --now hmailserver-update.path, which turns the apply off while the update check and download go on. Windows, builds with -DHM_LIVE_UPDATE=OFF and the container image are not affected.

- Progressive Robot Ltd / hMailServer: affected 6.3.4 <6.3.6 (semver)

### CVE-2026-104659 — Origin Validation Error in hMailServer
- Assigner: GitLab | Published: 2026-10-08 | Updated: 2026-10-08 | Max CVSS: 7.5

- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 7.5 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

Missing Host header validation and missing throttling of failed administrator sign-ins in the REST API listener of Progressive Robot hMailServer 6.0.0 through 6.3.5 allow a remote attacker to brute-force the server administrator's password through the administrator's own browser by DNS rebinding. The listener, which is off by default and bound to the loopback when enabled, answered requests whatever their Host header named, and a failed sign-in with the administrator's password from the loopback was neither auto-banned nor delayed. A web page whose host name the attacker rebinds to 127.0.0.1, opened in a browser on the server, can therefore send authenticated requests to the listener, read the answers and try administrator passwords at full speed until one is accepted, giving the attacker full administrative control of the mail server.

**solutions:** Upgrade to hMailServer 6.3.6, whose REST listener refuses an unexpected Host before any authentication and delays a wrong administrator password on every route. Until then: keep the REST API off (RestApiPort 0, the default) or reach it only through a reverse proxy that checks the Host header; give the administrator a long random password and enrol its second factor; do not browse the web from the server.

### CVE-2026-104660 — Missing Authorization in hMailServer
- Assigner: GitLab | Published: 2026-10-08 | Updated: 2026-10-08 | Max CVSS: 7.8
- CWE: CWE-862 CWE-862: Missing Authorization
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 7.8 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

Missing authorization on COM objects in Progressive Robot hMailServer 6.0.0 through 6.3.5 (Windows only) lets a local interactive user with no hMailServer credential read and write arbitrary files as the service account and queue mail as any sender. The service registers its COM classes with no DCOM access or launch permission and calls CoInitializeSecurity with no security descriptor, so any user logged on at the console or over Remote Desktop can activate the classes in the running service; a hMailServer.Message, its Attachments and Attachment, and a hMailServer.FetchAccount created this way carry a credential that never authenticated. Attachments.Add(path) and Attachment.SaveAs(path) performed no authorization check, and Message.Save/Copy and FetchAccount.AccountID/Save performed none either up to 6.3.3 and from 6.3.4 treated a holder with no credential as the server's own event-script host. Because the service does not impersonate the COM caller, Attachments.Add reads any file the service account can read and returns it, Attachment.SaveAs writes attacker-chosen bytes to any path it can write (on a LocalSystem installation, code execution as SYSTEM), Message.Save queues outbound mail from any address past the SMTP checks, and FetchAccount attaches a mail-fetch job to any mailbox. The objects an Application handed out behave the same once a later Authenticate on that Application fails.

**solutions:** Upgrade to hMailServer 6.3.6, whose COM API refuses a message or fetch account that carries no credential outside the server's own event scripts, serves and writes a file on the server's disk through a message to the server administrator alone, and adds Application.CreateMessage() so a signed-in program composes mail that carries its credential. Until then: Do not allow untrusted users to log on interactively (console or Remote Desktop) to the server host. There is no configuration switch that closes this before 6.3.6; restricting the DCOM AppID's launch/access permission to exclude INTERACTIVE would also close it.

Affected:
- Progressive Robot Ltd / hMailServer: affected 6.0.0 <6.3.6 (semver)

Credits: Found in the hMailServer project's own security review (Progressive Robot Ltd)

### CVE-2026-104704 — Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information in hMailServer
- Assigner: GitLab | Published: 2026-10-08 | Updated: 2026-10-08 | Max CVSS: 7.4
- CWE: CWE-319 CWE-319: Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 7.4 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

Progressive Robot hMailServer 6.0.0 through 6.3.5 does not enforce TLS for outbound SMTP delivery to a mail exchanger whose DNSSEC-validated TLSA records contain no DANE-EE (usage 3) record, contrary to RFC 7672 section 2.2. The server used only DANE-EE records and treated a validated TLSA record set consisting of DANE-TA (usage 2) or otherwise unusable records as if no records were published, so delivery to such a host fell back to opportunistic TLS. An attacker with an active position on the network path between the server and the recipient's mail exchanger can suppress or break the STARTTLS negotiation and cause messages to be delivered in cleartext, where they can be read and modified.

**solutions:** Upgrade to hMailServer 6.3.6, which verifies DANE-TA as well as DANE-EE records and requires TLS to a host whose validated TLSA records are all unusable. Until then, an SMTP route for each recipient domain concerned that names its mail exchangers with the connection security 'STARTTLS (required)' prevents delivery in cleartext to that domain.

- Progressive Robot Ltd / hMailServer: affected 6.0.0 <6.3.6 (semver)

### CVE-2026-105437 — Heap-based Buffer Overflow in Git
- Assigner: GitLab | Published: 2026-11-10 | Updated: 2026-11-16 | Max CVSS: 7.5
- CWE: CWE-122 CWE-122: Heap-based Buffer Overflow
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 7.5 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=poc, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total
- CVSS 3.1 (nvd:cve@gitlab.com:Secondary): 7.5 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`

Affected versions of Git have a heap buffer overflow in the three-way merge
code (xdiff), which an attacker can trigger through a repository they
control.

When Git merges a file, it first adds up the size of the merged
output, allocates a buffer of that size, and then writes the output into
it. That total was kept in a 32-bit signed integer. The
conflict-marker-size attribute, which can be set from a committed
.gitattributes file, accepts any positive integer, and the markers are
written several times for every conflict. A small file with a huge marker
size and many separate conflicts can therefore push the total past 4 GiB,
so the integer wraps to a small value and Git writes attacker-controlled
merge output past the end of a buffer that is too small. At minimum this
crashes Git, and because the overflow is large and its contents are largely
attacker-controlled, worse heap corruption is possible.

Any command that does a textual three-way merge can trigger it, such
as git-merge(1), git-rebase(1), git-cherry-pick(1), and
git-merge-tree(1). The latter is most likely a target for Git forges,
which might use git-merge-tree(1) on the server-side to check
mergeability. When the server reads attributes from trees in the
repository (for example through attr.tree or --attr-source), any
user who can push branches and request that they be merged (for
example by opening a pull or merge request) can trigger the overflow
without anyone else doing anything, and the data they push is small
because the oversized output only appears during the merge.

The problem has been patched by computing the size as size_t and
checking every addition for overflow, so Git stops with an error
instead of overflowing.

Servers that cannot upgrade right away can add

* conflict-marker-size=7

to each repository's info/attributes as a workaround, which overrides
any in-tree .gitattributes, or turn off server-side mergeability checks for
untrusted repositories.

### CVE-2026-107567 — Use of Less Trusted Source in hMailServer
- Assigner: GitLab | Published: 2026-10-19 | Updated: 2026-10-20 | Max CVSS: 7.5
- CWE: CWE-348 CWE-348: Use of Less Trusted Source
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 7.5 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=partial

Use of a less trusted source in the DKIM signing of Progressive Robot hMailServer 6.0.0 through 6.3.6 allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to have mail they write signed with the DKIM key of a domain the server hosts, so that it passes DKIM and DMARC for that domain at other receivers. With DKIM signing enabled for a hosted domain, the server signed every message on its first delivery pass as the domain named in its From header, before local delivery, whatever the message's origin and without checking that its sender had authenticated. A sender anywhere could therefore send the server, as ordinary inbound mail, a message whose From is any address at such a domain, and the server signed it with that domain's key. Every copy the server then sent on to an address outside carried a valid signature aligned with the forged From, whatever the domain's DMARC policy: an account's forward, a mail rule's forward or copy, a Sieve redirect, an alias or distribution list with an outside member, the mirror copy, a managed-list or journal copy, or a message released from quarantine. A signed copy can also be re-sent to other recipients while the domain's key is unchanged. Exploitation needs DKIM signing to be enabled for the hosted domain (it is off until configured) and, for the forgery to leave the server, a forward, alias, list or rule that carries the domain's mail to an outside address. The signer likewise signed a message submitted over authenticated SMTP as whatever hosted domain its From header named, a header authenticated SMTP does not hold to the submitting account, so that an account of one hosted domain could have mail written in the name of another hosted domain signed with that domain's key; this mattered where the server holds signed-in senders to their own envelope addresses (SmtpAuthenticatedSenderCheck, off by default), as the signature was then the remaining way for such mail to pass the other domain's DMARC policy.

**solutions:** Upgrade to hMailServer 6.3.7. It records on each message, and on every copy of it, whether the message came from outside: an SMTP session that did not authenticate and was not a submission the server's IP ranges allow without authentication, a download from an external account, or an imported file. It signs a message as its From domain only when an authenticated user submitted it (as another domain the server hosts only when the account may send as the address its From names), the server made it, or an IP range let it in as one of the server's own domains, so mail from outside and its forwards keep only the signatures they arrived with, and a signed-in account's message from an address at another hosted domain that the account may not send as is sent unsigned as that domain. Until then, do one of the following: publish a DMARC policy of quarantine or reject for each hosted domain the server signs for and set the server's DMARC failure score (DMARCFailureScore) at or above the spam delete threshold (SpamDeleteThreshold), so that such a message is refused on arrival; refuse it in an OnAcceptMessage event script when the client has not authenticated and the From header names a domain the server signs for; remove the forwards, rule forwards, Sieve redirects, alias and list members and mirror addresses that carry mail to outside addresses; or disable DKIM signing for the hosted domains, which alone of these also covers a signed-in account's submission. Rotate the DKIM key of any domain whose key may have signed forged mail.

Affected:
- Progressive Robot Ltd / hMailServer: affected 6.0.0 <=6.3.6 (semver)

Credits: Found in the hMailServer project's own security review (Progressive Robot Ltd)

References:
- https://gitlab.com/hmailserver/hmailserver/-/work_items/84
- https://gitlab.com/hmailserver/hmailserver/-/releases/v6.3.7

### CVE-2026-107569 — Unchecked Input for Loop Condition in hMailServer
- Assigner: GitLab | Published: 2026-10-19 | Updated: 2026-10-20 | Max CVSS: 7.5
- CWE: CWE-606 CWE-606: Unchecked Input for Loop Condition
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 7.5 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=partial

Unchecked input for a loop condition in Progressive Robot hMailServer 6.0.0 through 6.3.6 allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to stop the server carrying mail. The server bounds the mail it generates in response to a message - a rule forward, reply or copy, an account forward, a Sieve redirect, vacation or notify, a bounce, an out-of-office reply - by a counter it carries in the message's X-hMailServer-LoopCount header, and makes no more once the counter reaches the configured rule loop limit (5 by default); that is what ends a forwarding or auto-reply cycle in a bounded number of hops. X-hMailServer-LoopCount is an ordinary header that is not stripped from mail arriving from outside, and the server read it with a signed conversion and no validation, so a count below zero passed every test against the limit: a sender who sets X-hMailServer-LoopCount to a negative value, or on the Linux builds to a value above the 32-bit signed range that the conversion wraps to a negative one, lifts the bound, and a message that enters a generated-mail cycle then loops up to about two thousand million times, each hop a queued message and a delivery, filling the queue and disk and stopping mail service. The Sieve notify action (from 6.2.22) consulted no limit at all, and its increment of the count could overflow a signed integer; and an account could reset the counter on its own mail through a Sieve editheader of the header (from 6.2.22) or a rule Set header value action (all versions) ahead of a forward or redirect.

**solutions:** Upgrade to hMailServer 6.3.7, which reads X-hMailServer-LoopCount in one validated place (a count only when it is digits and never above the limit; anything else is read as the limit so no generated mail is made from it), holds a Sieve notify to the same limit, and refuses an account Sieve script or rule that edits the counter, and writes a line break in a header value as spaces unless it folds the line, so that no value a generated message is built from writes a field of its own. Until then there is no setting that stops the header being read or that turns Sieve off: reduce forwarding and auto-reply arrangements that can feed one another, keep the Sieve script surfaces closed to accounts (ManageSieveServerPort=0, the default, and the REST API off where it is not needed, RestApiPort=0, the default), review active Sieve scripts and account rules for a notify of the account's own address and for an edit of X-hMailServer-LoopCount, and watch the queue for a message generated far past the loop limit.

Affected:
- Progressive Robot Ltd / hMailServer: affected 6.0.0 <=6.3.6 (semver)

Credits: Found in the hMailServer project's own security review (Progressive Robot Ltd)

References:
- https://gitlab.com/hmailserver/hmailserver/-/work_items/81
- https://gitlab.com/hmailserver/hmailserver/-/releases/v6.3.7

### CVE-2026-107571 — Incorrect Default Permissions in hMailServer
- Assigner: GitLab | Published: 2026-10-19 | Updated: 2026-10-20 | Max CVSS: 7.8
- CWE: CWE-276 CWE-276: Incorrect Default Permissions
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 7.8 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

Incorrect default permissions in the Windows installer of Progressive Robot hMailServer 6.0.0 through 6.3.6 allow a local authenticated user to run code as the mail server's high-privileged accounts when the product is installed in a folder whose permissions are inherited from a writable parent, such as the root of a drive. The installer places the server's programs in the Bin folder of the program folder and gives neither the program folder nor Bin any permissions of their own, so they inherit the parent's. Under the default location, Program Files, ordinary users receive only read and execute and the configuration is not affected; but the installer accepts any path without warning, and a program folder at the root of an NTFS volume inherits write access for a broad group - Authenticated Users (Modify) on a Windows client, Users (create files and folders) on Windows Server. A local user without administrator rights can then alter or replace the service program, which runs as LocalSystem or as the service's virtual account, or the programs an administrator runs elevated from Bin during setup and maintenance, or place a library in Bin that those programs load in place of the system copy, gaining code execution with those privileges. The default Program Files installation is not affected.

**solutions:** Upgrade to hMailServer 6.3.7. Its hMailServer.exe /ProtectFolders, which setup runs at the end of every server installation and upgrade, gives the program folder, Bin and ControlPanel SYSTEM and the Administrators full control and Users read and execute (where every user could read the folder), nothing inherited, and, where another account owned one of them, makes the Administrators its owner and takes away that folder's own entries that let others change it; setup also gives a program folder it creates those permissions before it copies anything into it, and hardens, before its files, the existing folder of an installation of the Control Panel alone. 6.3.7 does not yet create a new program folder with those permissions already in place, harden the folder before setup's own steps on an upgrade, a repair or a server installation into a folder that already existed, refuse a link or junction on the program folder's path (it is logged), or list the files in Bin and ControlPanel by owner. Before upgrading an affected installation, or until it is upgraded, follow from an elevated Command Prompt the steps in the hMailServer documentation, ServiceAccount.md, "Before upgrading an installation at a drive's root": first note who owns the program folder and what is directly in it (dir /q /a "<folder>") and everything in Bin, ControlPanel, Events, WebAdmin, DBScripts, Addons and Languages (dir /q /s /a); then, for the program folder, then Bin, then ControlPanel, make the Administrators its owner (icacls "<folder>" /setowner *S-1-5-32-544, the folder alone, without /T); take away every entry of the folder's own but SYSTEM's, the Administrators' and deny entries, one account a line (icacls "<folder>" /remove:g: the Users' and the service's by their SIDs, the service's only where the server is installed; the two application package groups by theirs, *S-1-15-2-1 and *S-1-15-2-2; anybody else's by the name icacls lists; and an entry icacls lists by a SID that names no account with the documentation's PowerShell line); replace what it inherits (icacls "<folder>" /inheritance:r /grant:r *S-1-5-18:(OI)(CI)F *S-1-5-32-544:(OI)(CI)F *S-1-5-32-545:(OI)(CI)RX); and on Bin and ControlPanel, where the server is installed, give the service account back its read and execute - each icacls line reporting "Successfully processed 1 files"; or move the installation under Program Files. Reinstall the programs into a new folder that only the administrators may change, not over the installation, where accounts that are not administrators could sign in while the installation was exposed, where another account made the program folder or could change it before the installation, where anybody but SYSTEM, the Administrators or TrustedInstaller owned the program folder, a file directly in it, or Bin, ControlPanel, Events, WebAdmin, DBScripts, Addons or Languages or anything in them, or where one of the three folders had an entry of its own that let another account change it, or one the steps could not take away: setup leaves in place every file it does not ship, and puts the event script, which the service runs, and the scripts in Addons only where none is there, so read the old event script before copying it. Setup run into a folder without a settings file sets up a new, empty server there, so the settings file and the data go into the new folder first (ServiceAccount.md, "Reinstalling into a new folder"): stop the service and run nothing from the old folder, its uninstaller included; copy, not move, the mail, the built-in database's folder and the settings file into the new folder, the copies kept private; read the copy of the settings file, deleting its AdministratorPassword and each [Directories] line with a path in the old folder; then, with a 32-bit installation's uninstall entry taken away, run the release's setup with the new folder; read in the new Control Panel the programs the database's settings name, make the REST API's keys again, change each path the database holds into the old folder, and, once nothing names it, delete the old folder by hand.

Affected:
- Progressive Robot Ltd / hMailServer: affected 6.0.0 <=6.3.6 (semver)

Credits: Found in the hMailServer project's own security review (Progressive Robot Ltd)

### CVE-2026-107573 — Incorrect Default Permissions in hMailServer
- Assigner: GitLab | Published: 2026-10-08 | Updated: 2026-10-08 | Max CVSS: 7.8
- CWE: CWE-276 CWE-276: Incorrect Default Permissions
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 7.8 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

Incorrect default permissions in the Windows installer of Progressive Robot hMailServer 6.0.0 through 6.3.5 allow a local authenticated user to read the mail server's data. The installer created the data, log, temp, database and event folders and the hMailServer.INI configuration file with the permissions inherited from the installation folder, by default under Program Files, which give the local Users group read access. Any user who can sign in to the computer could read every stored message, the logs, the built-in database with the accounts' password hashes whenever the service is stopped, and the configuration file, including the database password, which is sealed only with the machine's DPAPI key and can be unsealed by any local account; with an external database that password gives full control of it. The Linux AppImage of 6.3.0 through 6.3.5 likewise created its per-user data folders readable by other local users.

**solutions:** Upgrade to hMailServer 6.3.6, whose installer makes the data, log, temp, database and event folders and hMailServer.INI private to SYSTEM, the Administrators and the service at every installation and upgrade; then change the database password and the administrator password if accounts that are not administrators could sign in to the server. Until then, from an elevated prompt, remove the inherited entries for Users and the application package groups from those folders and the file with icacls (/inheritance:d, then /remove:g).

Affected:
- Progressive Robot Ltd / hMailServer: affected 6.0.0 <6.3.6 (semver)

### CVE-2026-107574 — Inefficient Algorithmic Complexity in hMailServer
- Assigner: GitLab | Published: 2026-10-08 | Updated: 2026-10-08 | Max CVSS: 7.5
- CWE: CWE-407 CWE-407: Inefficient Algorithmic Complexity
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 7.5 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=partial

Inefficient algorithmic complexity in the JSON reader of Progressive Robot hMailServer allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to make the mail services unavailable. Reading a JSON object kept the first of each duplicated member name by searching the members already read, so an object of N distinct member names cost O(N^2): 1 MB took 8.9 seconds and 4 MB took 300 seconds against the affected code. A remote attacker reaches the reader without an account by mailing a crafted TLS-RPT report (up to 16 MB after decompression) to a hosted domain's published report mailbox, which is read on a delivery thread; a few such reports hold every delivery thread (ten by default), so the server delivers no mail, local or outbound, for over an hour per report. A signed-in account reaches the same 16 MB body through the webmail's own REST routes, holding the REST API's own worker threads. Where no report mailbox is configured, the unauthenticated REST sign-in routes that read a JSON body are capped at 64 KB and are not affected.

**solutions:** Upgrade to hMailServer 6.3.6, which keeps the member names seen in a hash set, so a JSON object is read in one pass. Until then, where domain reports are on, move the report mailbox off a hosted domain; restart the service to end a busy thread.

Affected:
- Progressive Robot Ltd / hMailServer: affected 6.2.28 <6.3.6 (semver)

Credits: Found in the hMailServer project's own security review (Progressive Robot Ltd)

- https://gitlab.com/hmailserver/hmailserver/-/work_items/76
- https://gitlab.com/hmailserver/hmailserver/-/releases/v6.3.6

### CVE-2026-107576 — Inefficient Algorithmic Complexity in hMailServer
- Assigner: GitLab | Published: 2026-10-08 | Updated: 2026-10-08 | Max CVSS: 7.5
- CWE: CWE-407 CWE-407: Inefficient Algorithmic Complexity
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 7.5 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=partial

Inefficient algorithmic complexity in the inbound DKIM and ARC signature verification of Progressive Robot hMailServer 6.0.0 through 6.3.5 allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to make the mail services unavailable by sending a message. Building the canonical header and choosing the header fields named in a signature's h= tag took time growing with the square of the message's header: the 'simple' canonicalisation prepended each continuation line of a folded field to the lines already gathered, and both canonicalisations searched the gathered fields from the bottom for each h= name and erased the match from the middle of the list. A message whose header holds very many fields, or a field folded over very many lines, with a DKIM-Signature the attacker signs for a domain they control, keeps a worker thread busy for tens of seconds per signature; up to ten signatures are evaluated per message by each of the DKIM and DMARC tests, on the threads that serve delivery and SMTP.

**solutions:** Upgrade to hMailServer 6.3.6, which builds the canonical header in one pass and chooses the h= fields from an index by name. Until then, lower the maximum message size, which bounds the cost.

- Progressive Robot Ltd / hMailServer: affected 6.0.0 <6.3.6 (semver)

### CVE-2026-107577 — Loop with Unreachable Exit Condition ('Infinite Loop') in hMailServer
- Assigner: GitLab | Published: 2026-10-08 | Updated: 2026-10-08 | Max CVSS: 7.5
- CWE: CWE-835 CWE-835: Loop with Unreachable Exit Condition ('Infinite Loop')
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 7.5 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=partial

Inefficient algorithmic complexity and a non-terminating loop in the MIME processing of received messages in Progressive Robot hMailServer 6.0.0 through 6.3.5 allow a remote unauthenticated attacker to make the mail services unavailable by sending a message. Removing a MIME header parameter whose value is empty and directly followed by a semicolon (for example a Content-Disposition with 'filename=a.bat; filename=;') entered a loop that never terminates, holding a worker thread at full load until the server is restarted; this is reached when the attachment blocker renames a blocked attachment or a filename is set over the REST API. Separately, decoding a header field that holds many RFC 2047 encoded words of an encoding other than base64 or quoted-printable, removing a parameter with many RFC 2231 continuations, and deleting many header fields of one name each took time growing with the square of the message, on the small thread pools that serve IMAP, SMTP and POP3 connections, delivery and the REST API.

**solutions:** Upgrade to hMailServer 6.3.6, which removes a MIME parameter and deletes header fields in a single pass and searches an encoded word's terminator only for a decodable word. Until then: lower the maximum message size (which bounds the quadratic paths but not the non-terminating one), and restart the service to end a hung thread.

### CVE-2026-107579 — Inefficient Algorithmic Complexity in hMailServer
- Assigner: GitLab | Published: 2026-10-08 | Updated: 2026-10-08 | Max CVSS: 7.5
- CWE: CWE-407 CWE-407: Inefficient Algorithmic Complexity
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 7.5 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=partial

Inefficient algorithmic complexity in the bounce and complaint processing of Progressive Robot hMailServer 6.3.4 and 6.3.5 allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to stop mail delivery by sending messages, when bounce processing or complaint processing is enabled or a mailing list is managed by the server (none is by default). The readers of incoming delivery status notifications (RFC 3464) and abuse feedback reports (RFC 5965) removed the blank lines at the start of the returned headers part two bytes at a time, copying the rest of the part each time, so their work grew with the square of the number of blank lines. A message shaped like such a report, whose headers part begins with a very large number of blank lines within the reader's 2 MB limit, keeps a delivery thread busy for over a minute while it is delivered, and a few such messages a minute keep every delivery thread busy.

**solutions:** Upgrade to hMailServer 6.3.6, whose report readers cut the leading blank lines off once. Until then, turn bounce processing, complaint processing and list management off (the default).

### CVE-2026-107584 — Not Failing Securely ('Failing Open') in hMailServer
- Assigner: GitLab | Published: 2026-10-08 | Updated: 2026-10-08 | Max CVSS: 7.4
- CWE: CWE-636 CWE-636: Not Failing Securely ('Failing Open')
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 7.4 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

Progressive Robot hMailServer 6.0.0 through 6.3.5 fails open when applying DANE (RFC 7672) to outbound SMTP delivery. The server's validating DNSSEC resolver treated a TLSA or MX lookup that did not complete (no answer, SERVFAIL, a malformed reply), an answer without the requested records and without an NSEC/NSEC3 proof of their absence, and an answer whose records carried no applicable RRSIG as if the recipient domain were unsigned, and from 6.2.19 it also delivered to mail exchangers taken from an unvalidated MX lookup that the DNSSEC-validated MX record set did not name. An attacker who can drop, forge or strip DNS answers on the path to the server's resolver, at the resolver, or between the resolver and the recipient domain's name servers, and who holds an active position on the SMTP path, can thereby disable DANE for a DNSSEC-signed recipient domain and cause messages to be delivered in cleartext or to a host of the attacker's choosing with an arbitrary certificate, where they can be read and modified.

**solutions:** Upgrade to hMailServer 6.3.6, which treats an incomplete, unsigned or unproven DNSSEC answer for a TLSA or MX lookup under a signed zone as indeterminate, does not use a mail exchanger whose lookup was indeterminate, defers the delivery when none is left, delivers only to mail exchangers named by a DNSSEC-validated MX record set, and (for a host whose DNS servers are IPv6 only) asks those IPv6 servers. Until then, for each recipient domain whose mail must be protected, an SMTP route that names its mail exchangers with the connection security 'STARTTLS (required)', with remote certificate verification on (VerifyRemoteSslCertificate=1), prevents delivery in cleartext or to another host for that domain; and the server's DNS resolver should be one reached over a trusted path, such as a validating resolver on the same host.

- Progressive Robot Ltd / hMailServer: affected 6.0.0 <6.3.6 (semver)

### CVE-2026-114476 — Incorrect Authorization in hMailServer
- Assigner: GitLab | Published: 2026-10-21 | Updated: 2026-10-29 | Max CVSS: 7.5
- CWE: CWE-863 CWE-863: Incorrect Authorization
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 7.5 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

Incorrect authorization in the REST administration API of Progressive Robot hMailServer 6.3.4 through 6.3.6 allows a remote authenticated user whose credential holds the manage_roles permission in named domains - a full-scope API key issued for those domains, or an account assigned the serveradmin role with a list of domains - to obtain the server administrator's authority. An account's admin level gives it authority, and a role assigned to it replaces that authority, which is how an administrator narrows an account whose admin level is the server administrator's. The route that takes a role away (DELETE /api/v1/role-assignments/{address}) checked only that the credential takes in what the account held at the time, not what it would hold afterwards, so such a credential could take a narrowing role away from an account in its domains whose admin level is the server administrator's, returning it to the server administrator's authority, and, having set that account's password while it held the narrower role, sign in as the server administrator.

**solutions:** Upgrade to hMailServer 6.3.7, in which a role is given or taken away, over the REST and the COM APIs, only by a credential that holds manage_roles in the account's domain and takes in both what the account holds now and what it will hold afterwards - with no role left, the authority of its admin level - so a credential confined to named domains is refused taking a role away from an account whose admin level is the server administrator's. Until then, give an account that a role narrows the admin level its role intends rather than the server administrator's, do not issue a full-scope API key, or assign serveradmin, confined to named domains to a party not trusted with the whole server, and review the role assignments and the accounts whose admin level is the server administrator's (after upgrading as well, since an upgrade does not give back a role already taken away).

Affected:
- Progressive Robot Ltd / hMailServer: affected 6.3.4 <=6.3.6 (semver)

Credits: Found in the hMailServer project's own security review (Progressive Robot Ltd)

References:
- https://gitlab.com/hmailserver/hmailserver/-/work_items/88
- https://gitlab.com/hmailserver/hmailserver/-/releases/v6.3.7

### CVE-2026-114489 — Missing Authorization in hMailServer
- Assigner: GitLab | Published: 2026-10-21 | Updated: 2026-10-29 | Max CVSS: 8.1
- CWE: CWE-862 CWE-862: Missing Authorization
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 8.1 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

Missing authorization in the REST and COM administration APIs of Progressive Robot hMailServer 6.0.0 through 6.3.6 allows a remote authenticated user whose credential is confined to named domains to change mail routing and domain configuration beyond those domains on a multi-tenant server. A domain administrator, an account or API key given another role that manages accounts in named domains, or a full-scope API key issued for named domains could create a domain alias for any name (so that other tenants' mail for that name is diverted to an address the attacker controls, or denied), rename a domain to any name the server does not host, set a rule's bind-to-address, send-using-route or script-function action to reach one of the server's own addresses, a configured route's stored credentials or a function of the server's event script, and set the domain's relay host - which delivery then connects to with no address rule - to an address on the server's own network; and over the COM API any account could set the three rule actions on its own rules, where the script-function action runs at delivery. The authorization gate did not refuse these routes to a confined credential and the handlers were not given the caller; over COM the domain-alias save performed no authorization check at all, the domain rename required only a domain administrator, and a rule save required at most that the caller could change the rule's owner.

**solutions:** Upgrade to hMailServer 6.3.7, which refuses the domain-alias create, the domain rename and an internal relay host to a credential that is confined to named domains, and the reaching rule actions (bind-to-address, send-using-route, script-function on an owned rule) to anyone but the server administrator, over both the REST and the COM APIs, while keeping the changes that stay inside the credential's domains. Until then, on a multi-tenant server, do not give a domain-administrator credential, a role that manages accounts in named domains, or a named-domain API key to a party not trusted with the whole server; keep the REST API off (RestApiPort=0, the default) where it is not needed; and review existing domain aliases, domain names, relay hosts and account/domain rule actions for entries a confined credential should not have made, and the accounts' own rules for these three actions, which withholding such credentials does not stop an account setting on its own rules over COM (do this after upgrading as well, since an upgrade does not undo a change already made).

Affected:
- Progressive Robot Ltd / hMailServer: affected 6.0.0 <=6.3.6 (semver)

Credits: Found in the hMailServer project's own security review (Progressive Robot Ltd)

References:
- https://gitlab.com/hmailserver/hmailserver/-/work_items/86
- https://gitlab.com/hmailserver/hmailserver/-/releases/v6.3.7

### CVE-2026-114490 — Incorrect Authorization in hMailServer
- Assigner: GitLab | Published: 2026-10-21 | Updated: 2026-10-29 | Max CVSS: 7.8
- CWE: CWE-863 CWE-863: Incorrect Authorization
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 7.8 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

Incorrect authorization in the COM administration API of Progressive Robot hMailServer 6.3.4 through 6.3.6 allows an account assigned the serveradmin role with a list of domains - a credential an administrator may create meaning to confine it to those domains - to act as the whole-server administrator over COM. Administrator roles are meant to confine such a credential to the domains its list names, and the REST API did not take it for the server administrator, but the COM API's server-administrator check read the administer_server permission as the whole server whatever list the grant carried. So the credential signed in through the Control Panel, or through a script run on the server, as the server administrator of every domain: it could read and change every domain's accounts and mail, rename any domain, map a domain alias onto any, write the server's settings and secrets, and create further server-administrator accounts. The COM API's domain-administrator check, asked with no domain, likewise let an account assigned the domainadmin role with a list of domains that leaves out the account's own domain administer that domain's ordinary accounts over COM. An account holding serveradmin with no list is the server administrator by design and is unaffected, as are the help desk, auditor and custom roles.

**solutions:** Upgrade to hMailServer 6.3.7, in which the one authorization rule answers administer_server only for a grant that reaches every domain, so an account assigned serveradmin with a list of domains is confined to the domains the list names, holding serveradmin's permissions in them short of what reaches beyond a domain and none in any other: over COM it is refused the server settings, a domain alias, a domain's name and the other changes that reach beyond a domain, exactly as over the REST API, where the same rule answers the check, and it is a domain administrator of its own account's domain where the list names that domain; it reaches the other domains its list names through REST, and over COM through the calls that name a domain of their own, among them the password reset, the unlock, the mailbox move and its history, the message trace, role assignment and a message's sender (send-as). An account assigned domainadmin with a list of domains likewise administers its own account's domain over COM only where the list names that domain. A grant with no list of domains is unchanged. Until then, do not assign the serveradmin role with a list of domains to a credential that must be confined: assign a custom role holding only the permissions it needs, with the list of domains, or the domainadmin role with a list of domains that names the account's own domain.

Affected:
- Progressive Robot Ltd / hMailServer: affected 6.3.4 <=6.3.6 (semver)

Credits: Found in the hMailServer project's own security review (Progressive Robot Ltd)

References:
- https://gitlab.com/hmailserver/hmailserver/-/work_items/87
- https://gitlab.com/hmailserver/hmailserver/-/releases/v6.3.7

### CVE-2026-126607 — Uncontrolled Search Path Element in hMailServer
- Assigner: GitLab | Published: 2026-11-11 | Updated: 2026-11-16 | Max CVSS: 7.8
- CWE: CWE-427 CWE-427: Uncontrolled Search Path Element
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 7.8 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total
- CVSS 3.1 (nvd:cve@gitlab.com:Secondary): 7.8 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`

Progressive Robot hMailServer 6.2.3 through 6.3.7 on Windows, with a MySQL or MariaDB database, hands the bundled MariaDB Connector/C the folder of its authentication plugins (the plugin folder in the installation's Bin folder) as Latin-1 bytes, which the client reads in the system's ANSI code page when it builds a plugin's path and loads the plugin with LoadLibraryExA, which allows a local authenticated user to execute code as the hMailServer service's account (LocalSystem, or the service's virtual account for a new installation from 6.3.4) by creating the folder those bytes name in the code page and placing in it a DLL with a plugin's name, when the installation folder's path holds a character between U+0080 and U+00FF whose byte the code page reads as another character, and none above U+00FF, and the user can create that other folder (by default any authenticated user may create a folder directly under the root of the system drive). The server converted the path with the C runtime's wcstombs_s in the C locale, which writes each character up to U+00FF as the byte of the same value: on code page 1252 those bytes are the same letters, while on another code page, such as 1251, or on a UTF-8 code page, they name another folder. The client loads the plugin the database server names in its greeting, unless it is built in, and any plugin the server names in an authentication switch, and tries again at each connection while a load fails, so with a MySQL 8.0 or later server, whose greeting names caching_sha2_password by default, the DLL is loaded at the next connection the service makes, whatever plugin the database account uses; a DLL's entry point runs when it is loaded. A path holding any character above U+00FF was handed over as an empty string, whatever the code page, from which the client makes a plugin's name at the root of the current drive: for the service, whose current folder is System32, that is the root of the system drive, where by default only administrators can create a file, but the server's own database commands (hMailServer.exe --check-database, --upgrade-database and the others from 6.3.4, and the /Debug and /Test console modes from 6.2.3) run in the folder they are started from - the product tells administrators to run them from an elevated prompt in the Bin folder, and the setup of 6.3.4 and 6.3.5 ran two or three of them itself with the Bin folder as their working folder for a new installation with an external database - so a DLL that a local authenticated user placed under a plugin's name at the root of a drive other users may write, such as a FAT or exFAT volume, was loaded into the administrator's process at the command's first connection to a MySQL 8.0 or later server. 6.3.8 fixes both cases: it hands the folder in the code page's bytes or by its short (8.3) name, and where neither can be written, a folder under the Windows system folder that holds no plugin and that only administrators can create, or else refuses the connection before attempting it; it never hands the empty value or a folder the current drive completes. The configuration is not the default: the default installation folder, under Program Files, is ASCII. Linux builds set no plugin folder and are not affected.

**solutions:** Upgrade to hMailServer 6.3.8, which on Windows always hands the bundled client its plugin folder in the bytes the client reads it in - the ANSI code page, or UTF-8 where that is the code page - or, where the code page lacks a character of the path, by the folder's short (8.3) name, which is the same folder; where neither can be written, it hands a folder under the Windows system folder that holds no plugin and that only administrators can create, so that a plugin found only in the installation's plugin folder is not loaded and the connection's error says why, and where even that folder cannot be written, it refuses the connection before attempting it, with error HM7537 in the log. It never hands Latin-1 bytes, the empty value or a folder the current drive or folder completes: that closes the service's case and the database commands' case alike. Before 6.3.8, install hMailServer in a folder whose path is ASCII alone, as the default folder under Program Files is, and start hMailServer.exe's database commands, and DBSetup when it finishes an installation, from a folder on the system drive. For a new installation of 6.3.4 or 6.3.5 with an external database, whose setup runs two or three of the commands in the Bin folder itself, only an installation folder whose path is ASCII avoids it. An installation whose path is ASCII is not affected; on a system whose code page for non-Unicode programs is 1252, the service is not affected unless the path holds a C1 control character (U+0080 to U+009F) whose byte code page 1252 reads as another character, but before 6.3.8 a path holding a character above U+00FF reaches a database command started from another drive on any code page. Setting MARIADB_PLUGIN_DIR in the service's environment does not help, since the client takes the option first and every affected version sets it.

Affected:
- Progressive Robot Ltd / hMailServer: affected 6.2.3 <=6.3.7 (semver)

Credits: Found by the hMailServer project (Progressive Robot Ltd)

References:
- https://gitlab.com/hmailserver/hmailserver/-/work_items/116
- https://gitlab.com/hmailserver/hmailserver/-/releases/v6.3.8

### CVE-2026-126609 — Improper Certificate Validation in hMailServer
- Assigner: GitLab | Published: 2026-11-11 | Updated: 2026-11-17 | Max CVSS: 7.5
- CWE: CWE-295 CWE-295: Improper Certificate Validation
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 7.5 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total
- CVSS 3.1 (nvd:cve@gitlab.com:Secondary): 7.5 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`

Progressive Robot hMailServer 6.2.25 through 6.3.7 on Windows, with a PostgreSQL database, the connection's sslmode require, verify-ca or verify-full, and a root certificate file named by PostgreSQLSslRootCert (from 6.2.25) or, with TlsMode=verify-full and neither PostgreSQL key set, by TlsCaFile (from 6.3.4), hands the file's name to libpq as bytes in the system's ANSI code page (up to 6.3.5 as Latin-1 bytes, which on code page 1252 are the code page's own for U+00A0 to U+00FF), and libpq looks for the file by those bytes and then hands the same bytes to OpenSSL, whose file opening on Windows reads a name as UTF-8 first and opens the file at that reading when one is there. When every byte of the name outside ASCII also reads as UTF-8 - for example U+00C3 U+00A9, the bytes C3 A9 on code page 1252, which are U+00E9 in UTF-8 - the database server's certificate was checked against the file at that other name whenever one was there, which allows a local attacker who can create that file but cannot change the configured one, as any user can by default beside a file an administrator keeps under ProgramData, or beside a folder directly under the system drive's root whose permissions the administrator restricted, and who can intercept the connection to the database server or stand in for it, to have hMailServer trust a certificate authority of the attacker's own and read and modify the traffic between hMailServer and its database, the database password included; the file alone, holding no authority that issued the database server's certificate, stops hMailServer from connecting to its database. The same applies in 6.3.4 through 6.3.7 to TlsCaFile when an Oracle MySQL client library has been put in place of the bundled MariaDB Connector/C, since that client opens the file through OpenSSL in the same way; the bundled MariaDB Connector/C opens the file in the code page and is not affected, and neither are the Linux builds. The configuration is not the default: by default no root certificate file is named.

**solutions:** Upgrade to hMailServer 6.3.8, which on Windows refuses before connecting, with HM7534 in the error log, a root certificate file name whose bytes in the code page outside ASCII also read as UTF-8, for PostgreSQLSslRootCert and TlsCaFile alike and whichever database client is loaded, and hands an Oracle MySQL client the name in UTF-8, which names the same file. Until then, name the root certificate file by a path in ASCII alone, which reads as the same name in the code page and in UTF-8 and which every affected version hands over unchanged; where a name outside ASCII must stay, make sure no one else can create the file or folder that the name's UTF-8 reading names.

### CVE-2026-126610 — Improper Certificate Validation in hMailServer
- Assigner: GitLab | Published: 2026-11-11 | Updated: 2026-11-17 | Max CVSS: 7.4
- CWE: CWE-295 CWE-295: Improper Certificate Validation
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 7.4 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total
- CVSS 3.1 (nvd:cve@gitlab.com:Secondary): 7.4 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N`

Progressive Robot hMailServer 6.3.4 through 6.3.7, with a MySQL or MariaDB database and TlsMode=verify-full, does not hand the database client the CA file that TlsCaFile names when the file's name contains a character outside ASCII on Linux, or above U+00FF on Windows, which allows an attacker who can intercept the connection to the database server to read and modify the traffic between hMailServer and its database, by presenting, with MariaDB Connector/C 3.4.2 to 3.4.10 as the client, a certificate from any authority, its own included, for any name, and otherwise a certificate for the database server's name issued by any certificate authority in the system's trust store. The server converted the name for the client with the C runtime's conversion in the C locale, which gives an empty string for such a name, and then set no CA file at all, without an error, while certificate verification stayed on, so the client - MariaDB Connector/C, bundled on Windows and the distribution's on Linux - verified the certificate of a database server over the network against the system's trust store instead of the configured CA; Connector/C 3.4.2 to 3.4.10 (bundled on Windows in 6.3.4 to 6.3.6) went further and, with no CA file, took a certificate within its dates whose issuer it could not find, for any name, with neither its chain nor its name checked and no password proof, when the server offered first a sign-in method that hashes the password, which an attacker in the middle chooses (MariaDB's CONC-853, fixed in Connector/C 3.4.11), and Connector/C 3.4 accepted from a MariaDB 11.4 or later server a certificate the store did not vouch for when that server proved it held the account's password; on a connection it treats as local (127.0.0.1, ::1, a Unix socket, a named pipe, and localhost on Windows), Connector/C 3.4.1 and later checked neither the certificate's issuer nor its name, so that a local attacker able to stand in for the database server could present any certificate within its dates of its own making. The settings line of hmailserver --check-database still named the configured file, and the application log said the certificate had been checked. With MariaDB Connector/C 3.4.1 to 3.4.9 as the client - bundled on Windows in 6.3.4 to 6.3.6, and the client of Linux distributions that have not patched it - the missing CA file also met the precondition of CVE-2026-107819, so that a certificate issued for any other name by a trusted authority was enough to obtain the database password. On Linux the file was found only when the server ran on glibc under a locale whose character set holds the name's characters (a UTF-8 locale, or a legacy 8-bit one the system has, in whose bytes the file is then named); with no locale, LC_ALL=C or a locale the system lacks, and on Alpine (musl), the connection failed instead. The configuration is not the default: TlsMode defaults to prefer, which checks no certificate.

**solutions:** Upgrade to hMailServer 6.3.8, which hands the database client the CA file's name in the encoding the client opens it in - UTF-8 on Linux whatever the locale, the ANSI code page on Windows - and refuses before connecting, with HM7534 in the error log, a name it cannot write so, never handing over an empty one. Until then, give TlsCaFile a path in ASCII alone, which every affected version hands to the client as it is; on these versions the settings line of hmailserver --check-database names the configured file whether or not the client was given it, so it does not show the difference. On Linux, also update the distribution's MariaDB Connector/C to 3.4.11 or later, which fixes both CVE-2026-107819 and CONC-853, where one is offered; a version with the fix for CVE-2026-107819 alone still accepts a certificate whose issuer it cannot find.

### CVE-2026-126611 — Improper Certificate Validation in hMailServer

Progressive Robot hMailServer 6.3.4 through 6.3.7, with a MySQL or MariaDB database, TlsMode=verify-full and no TlsCaFile, does not verify the database server's certificate's issuer or name when the connection is one that MariaDB Connector/C treats as local - Server= set to 127.0.0.1, ::1 or localhost (on Linux a Unix socket), to . on Windows (a named pipe), or to a comma-separated list of servers that holds such an element - which allows a local attacker who can stand in for the database server, for example by listening on its port while it is stopped or restarting, to receive the database sign-in, the password included, and to read and modify the traffic between hMailServer and its database. hMailServer applied verify-full by turning the client's certificate verification on without a CA file, but MariaDB Connector/C 3.4.1 and later, on a connection they treat as local and with no CA file, accept any certificate within its validity period that is self-signed or sent with its own root, for any name (Connector/C 3.4.2 to 3.4.10 also one whose issuer they cannot find), so the client accepted the certificate an impostor made, asked no proof of the password and allowed a switch to an authentication method that sends the password unhashed, while hmailserver --check-database said the certificate had been checked against the system's trust store and the application log that it had been checked. The configuration is not the default: TlsMode defaults to prefer, which checks no certificate.

Until then, set TlsCaFile to a file holding only the CA that issues the database server's certificate, at a path in ASCII alone; the client then checks the certificate's issuer on such a connection, though not its name. On these versions the --check-database settings line and the application log say the certificate was checked either way, so they do not show the difference.

### CVE-2026-126612 — Improper Link Resolution Before File Access ('Link Following') in hMailServer

- CWE: CWE-59 CWE-59: Improper Link Resolution Before File Access ('Link Following')

- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total
- CVSS 3.1 (nvd:cve@gitlab.com:Secondary): 7.8 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`

Improper link resolution in the Windows installer of Progressive Robot hMailServer 6.0.0 through 6.3.7 allows a local authenticated user to run code as the mail server's service account or as an administrator when the path to the program folder passes through a junction, a symbolic link or a mount point that the user controls or that every user may change, such as a junction made at the root of a drive, which takes the root's permissions, or through a folder that every user may rename. Setup installed the programs through any such link without first checking who controls it, or whether a folder above the program folder may be renamed, and the service is registered to run the programs by that path, so the programs are installed where a link another account controls leads, or that account can later make the path lead to a folder it controls; the service, which runs as LocalSystem or as its virtual account, and the programs administrators run from Bin are then started from there. 6.3.7's fix for CVE-2026-107571 does not cover this: its hardening of the program folder, Bin and ControlPanel does not change a folder reached through a link that the administrators do not alone control, and setup does not refuse such a path: it installs through the link and at most reports afterwards that the folders could not be hardened. The default installation under Program Files is not affected.

**solutions:** Upgrade to hMailServer 6.3.8, whose setup holds every folder from the root of the volume down to the program folder, Bin and ControlPanel open and, before anything changes, refuses with exit code 7 a junction, a symbolic link or a mount point on the way that anybody but SYSTEM, the Administrators and TrustedInstaller owns, may change or may remove - a junction made at a drive's root and left with the permissions the root hands down among them - and a folder on the way that another account may rename or remove, or empty, naming each with the icacls that deals with it. Until then, install hMailServer under Program Files, or at a path with no link on it below folders that only administrators may change. For a link that is meant to be on the path, make it the administrators' alone from an elevated Command Prompt - icacls "<link>" /L /setowner *S-1-5-32-544, then icacls "<link>" /L /inheritance:r /grant:r *S-1-5-18:F *S-1-5-32-544:F *S-1-5-32-545:RX - and check where it leads (dir /al of the folder that holds it); make the Administrators the owner of each folder above the program folder that other accounts may change, and take away their right to change it; then restart Windows. Where another account owned or could change such a link or folder while the installation was there, reinstall into a new folder as the hMailServer documentation, ServiceAccount.md, "Reinstalling into a new folder", says.

### CVE-2026-126613 — Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling in hMailServer
- Assigner: GitLab | Published: 2026-11-11 | Updated: 2026-11-17 | Max CVSS: 7.5
- CWE: CWE-770 CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 7.5 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=partial
- CVSS 3.1 (nvd:cve@gitlab.com:Secondary): 7.5 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`

Allocation of resources without limits in the JSON reader of Progressive Robot hMailServer 6.3.2 through 6.3.7 allows a remote attacker to exhaust the server's memory and hold its threads, making mail delivery, the REST API and the webmail unavailable. The reader built a tree of values far larger than the text it read, copying each value into every level above it, and set no bound on the number of values, so a single JSON document of many small values, within the 16 MB the server reads, raised the service's memory by about 2 GB and held one thread for seconds to minutes. From 6.3.4 a remote unauthenticated attacker reaches the reader by mailing such a document as a TLS-RPT report, up to 16 MB once decompressed, to a hosted domain's report mailbox, where an administrator has set one; it is read on a mail delivery thread (ten by default), and those threads deliver all mail, local and outbound. From 6.3.4 it is also reached without an account through the reply to a password-protected message, with the message's link alone, where the REST API is on (it is off by default) and a public base URL for such links is set; and by any account, from 6.3.2 through the webmail's send and draft routes and from 6.3.4 through its other routes granted 16 MB and the send API; the webmail's send, draft and settings routes parsed the body again for each member read. The REST API serves every request on four worker threads, in the process that also serves SMTP, IMAP and POP3, so a few such documents at once make it unavailable and can exhaust the machine's memory and end the whole service. This is a separate defect from CVE-2026-107574, the reader's handling of duplicate member names, fixed in 6.3.6.

**solutions:** Upgrade to hMailServer 6.3.8, whose JSON reader moves each value into its place rather than copying it, and in which a REST request body is parsed within the bounds before any handler reads it, and the shared member readers read that one parse; a REST request body is held to 100,000 values, 10,000 members in an object and 32 levels, and a mailed TLS-RPT report to 200,000 values, 10,000 members in an object and 32 levels, each refused at the first value past a bound; the reply to a password-protected message is held to 2 MB. Until then, on 6.3.4 to 6.3.7, clear each domain's report mailbox, or move it off the domains the server hosts, so that no report is read by the server; and switch OpenPGP in the webmail off (portal_enabled under /api/v1/settings/openpgp), and off for any domain or account that holds openpgp_portal_enabled on, which refuses the reply to a password-protected message before its body is parsed; clearing the public base URL is not enough, since links already made stay usable. For the routes that take an account or an API key, only limiting who can reach the REST API avoids it (RestApiPort 0, the default, turns it off), or a reverse proxy in front of it that holds request bodies well below 16 MB. Restarting the service ends a busy thread.

- Progressive Robot Ltd / hMailServer: affected 6.3.2 <=6.3.7 (semver)
